subject: Skyport launch — warmup entitlement & fallback plan
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@skyport.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Skyport launch — initial ask (warmup + temporary entitlement)

Team —

Quick summary: Skyport is planning a staged rollout starting 2027-07-01 for their new chat assistant. ETA for GA is two weeks after. They expect a steep warmup over 72 hours with a traffic spike on day+3. Elena attached an initial load profile (CSV).

We need product + infra confirmation on two things ASAP:
- Temporary entitlement (short-lived quota bump) to cover warmup window and the day+3 spike. Please recommend target RPS and token cap.
- A model fallback plan: Skyport wants best-effort quality and predictable latency. If we need to shed load, can we route to a cheaper quantized variant automatically? What defaults do we set?

Action items I think are required:
1) Product (Priya, Priyom): confirm acceptable fallback model family and whether any feature gating is needed (function calling, streaming) during fallback.
2) Infra (Rishi): feasible entitlement range + canary rollout window (48–72h?) and who to call at 2am PST if things degrade.
3) CS (Naomi): collect exact expected hourly traffic by endpoint from Skyport (Elena) — they said 250k token/hr baseline rising to 1.8M token/hr peak. Need CSV.

Elena — thanks for the load profile. If you can send expected calls/hour per endpoint (chat vs embeddings vs rerank) it helps us plan batching/kv-cache knobs.

Karthik
Account Lead — Redwood Inference
From: Elena Park <elena@skyport.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 10:01:14 -0400
Subject: Re: Skyport launch — initial ask (warmup + temporary entitlement)

Thanks Karthik — attaching the more granular traffic CSV (skyport-launch-load.csv). High level:
- Day 0 (soft launch): 250k tokens/hr aggregate
- Day 1–2 (ramp): linear to 800k tokens/hr
- Day 3 (promo): 1.6–2.0M tokens/hr sustained for ~6 hours

Endpoint split (approx): chat 78%, embeddings 12%, search/rerank 10%. Typical prompt length 120 tokens; replies average 220 tokens.

We rely on streaming for user-perceived latency on chat. Fallback to a faster but slightly lower-quality model is acceptable for 30–40% of requests if we can preserve 95th latencies under 600ms.

Let us know what you need from our side.

—Elena
Launch Ops — Skyport AI

Attachment: skyport-launch-load.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 14:08:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Skyport launch — initial ask (warmup + temporary entitlement)

Thanks Elena and Karthik — got the CSV and baseline numbers. I ran a quick model of expected token/s and adjusted for batching; preliminary ask below.

Product asks / clarifications (Priya / Priyom):
- Fallback family: suggest routing to rdw-open-4q (8-bit quantized) as primary fallback; keep rdw-open-4 as the quality-primary during canary. Confirm support for streaming on rdw-open-4q (we may need to fall back to chunked streaming if native streaming not identical).
- Feature gating: disable function-calling during fallback for 6h blocks unless we see errors; enable structured output only on primary model.

Quota/entitlement recommendation (Rishi):
- Temp entitlement window: 2027-07-01 00:00 UTC to 2027-07-04 00:00 UTC (72h)
- Soft cap: 1.0M tokens/hr sustained (for warmup)
- Peak cap (burstable): up to 2.2M tokens/hr with automatic throttling thresholds at 1.2M and 1.8M

Operational asks (Rishi / Infra playbook):
- Canary policy: 6h rolling canary with 10% of traffic at start, double every 6h. Revert threshold: 5xx rate >0.5% for 10m or 95th latency >750ms.
- Fallback routing: automatic at 1.2M sustained tokens/hr, tiered shed to rdw-open-4q at 30% then 50%.
- Escalation: page on-call infra after two consecutive revert events; include CS and account lead.

Naomi — I will draft the entitlement request once product confirms fallback viability. Also attaching a short entitlement form we can submit to capacity ops.

Naomi Feldman
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: entitlement-request-4982.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 16:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Skyport launch — entitlement and emergency playbook confirmed

All — we can support the requested window and caps with these caveats and actions:
- Entitlement ticket created (ET-4982). Capacity team will reserve the burst pool and mark routing rules.
- Confirmed automatic model fallback to rdw-open-4q with chunked streaming enabled; product to finalize function-calling gating by EOD tomorrow.
- Runbook updates: added the 6h canary cadence + revert thresholds to the Skyport runbook.
- On-call rotation: if revert triggers between 22:00–08:00 PST, page infra-oncall and notify Rishi (primary) and Naomi. Daytime contacts remain Karthik and Priyom.

Next steps:
1) Priya/Priyom: confirm function-calling gating behavior so I can close ET-4982.
2) Naomi: please confirm Skyport accepts the provisional flow (we'll include the burst caps and the shed percentages in the final entitlement doc).
3) Karthik: I will share the entitlement ticket link and a short checklist for your pre-launch rehearsal.

Rishi Malhotra
Principal Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
